attempts.summary: Configured OPNsense node1 to route between lan-a (10.60.1.0/24, opt1/vtnet1) and lan-b (10.60.2.0/24, opt2/vtnet2). Added static addressing on node2 (10.60.1.11) and node3 (10.60.2.12) with routes via node1, firewall pass rules on both new interfaces, and a manual/hybrid outbound NAT rule that SNATs traffic sourced from 10.60.1.0/24 egressing via opt2 to node1's lan-b address (10.60.2.1). Verified node2->node3 connections are observed by node3 as arriving from 10.60.2.1 (node1), while node3->node2 connections keep node3's real address. Restarted all three nodes one at a time (OPNsense native reboot, systemctl reboot for RHEL nodes), proved changed boot identity on each (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3), and re-verified the NAT/routing behavior and connectivity after each restart, plus a final full end-to-end re-test after all three nodes were rebooted.
